page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The memory allocation provides 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% at 2688.38. However, multi-core and parallel processing capabilities are more limited, as shown by a weak multi-core stress-ng score of 5388.66 and a poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 20.59 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large block reads and writes (44.77 GB/sec and 35.36 GB/sec respectively), but weak performance for small cached blocks. Cryptographic operations perform moderately well, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 4217.66 falling into the average tier, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n2d-standard-4 is suited for general-purpose workloads that require moderate memory and steady single-threaded compute performance. It is appropriate for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded tasks. However, it is less optimal for highly parallelized applications, intensive database operations, or large-scale software compilation due to its lower multi-core benchmark results. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU acceleration further defines its role as a standard utility instance rather than a high-performance database or machine learning node.

It provides 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core and a dedicated CPU allocation, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. While single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and text processing tasks that do not require heavy multi-threaded compute or high-speed local disk access.
